primitives.name: Kick Distance Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The back stands as far as he thinks it possible for the opposing half to kick, under the most favorable DIAGRAN 11.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'d_{kick}': 'feet', 'v_0': 'initial velocity of the kick (ft/s)', '\\theta': 'launch angle relative to ground (radians)', '\\mu': 'coefficient of air drag', '\\rho': 'air density'}
primitives.assumptions: Constant gravitational acceleration, quadratic air resistance, neglects spin effects, perfect knowledge of opponent's kicking ability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At high launch angles (> 70 degrees) or low initial velocities, kicks become parabolic and easily intercepted; optimal range occurs around 45 degrees.

primitives.name: Scrimmage Failure Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: The formation, after the two attempts to run have failed, is, however, quite different in respect to one halfback and the back.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{transition}': 'dimensionless transition probability', 'run_1': 'Boolean indicator for first running attempt success', 'run_2': 'Boolean indicator for second running attempt success'}
primitives.assumptions: Markovian assumption that transition depends only on immediate prior failures, constant defensive response time, and opponent reacts deterministically to failure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When both running attempts fail with high confidence, the system enters a "recovery" phase where defenders retreat to prevent long kicks; this triggers a singular perturbation in the game dynamics.
